questions.prompt: Explain how semantic colors adapt between Light Mode and Dark Mode in iOS. Why is hardcoding hex colors discouraged?
questions.modelAnswer: Semantic colors like `UIColor.systemBackground` and `UIColor.label` resolve dynamically to appropriate palette values based on the active trait collection. In Light Mode, backgrounds appear light and labels appear dark; in Dark Mode, the palette inverts with elevated background contrast. Hardcoding hex colors like pure black or white prevents adaptive switching, causing illegible text and blinding backgrounds when the appearance changes.

rubric.criterion: Explains semantic colors resolve dynamically to light or dark shades based on the active trait collection.
Explains hardcoded colors fail to adapt and cause contrast and legibility bugs in opposite appearances.

questions.prompt: What steps are required to make a `UILabel` properly support Dynamic Type in UIKit?
questions.modelAnswer: First, assign a scalable text style using `UIFont.preferredFont(forTextStyle:)` rather than a fixed point size. Second, set `label.adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory = true` so the font updates when users change system size settings. Third, set `label.numberOfLines = 0` and remove fixed height constraints so the label can expand vertically and wrap text across multiple lines.

rubric.criterion: Mentions using UIFont.preferredFont and setting adjustsFontForContentSizeCategory to true.
Explains setting numberOfLines to 0 and removing fixed height constraints to prevent clipping.

questions.prompt: How does `@ScaledMetric` improve SwiftUI interfaces when users enable accessibility text sizes?
questions.modelAnswer: Standard Dynamic Type scales text views automatically, but non-text interface elements like image frames, icons, and layout padding remain fixed. The `@ScaledMetric` property wrapper scales custom numeric values proportionally with a chosen text style. This keeps non-text assets visually balanced alongside enlarged text instead of leaving icons disproportionately small.

rubric.criterion: Explains non-text elements like icons and padding do not scale automatically with text styles.
Explains @ScaledMetric scales numeric dimensions relative to a text style for visual balance.

questions.prompt: What problems arise when layouts use fixed height constraints with Dynamic Type, and how should layouts adapt?
questions.modelAnswer: Fixed height constraints prevent text containers from expanding vertically when fonts scale up, resulting in truncated words and clipped text. To resolve this, developers should remove fixed heights and rely on intrinsic content size. Additionally, when horizontal rows run out of space at accessibility sizes, layouts should switch to vertical stacks using `ViewThatFits` or by checking `isAccessibilitySize`.

rubric.criterion: Explains fixed heights cut off and truncate enlarged typography.
Describes removing fixed heights, using intrinsic sizing, and switching horizontal layouts to vertical stacks.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between `traitCollectionDidChange` and `registerForTraitChanges` in iOS 17+.
questions.modelAnswer: `traitCollectionDidChange` was deprecated in iOS 17 because it ran on every global trait change, forcing developers to manually inspect which traits changed. The modern replacement is `registerForTraitChanges`, which lets views subscribe directly to specific traits like `systemTraitsAffectingColorAppearance`. It executes closures only when specified traits change and safely provides `self: Self` without needing weak self captures.

rubric.criterion: Explains traitCollectionDidChange is deprecated and registerForTraitChanges targets specific traits.
Notes closures execute only when specified traits change and avoid retain cycles safely.
